notes:
- The app has a bar of its own now: Home, Library, and your profile: Everything the app does that is about you rather than about one title now lives on a page you can reach from one place. A floating capsule sits at the bottom of the main pages with three stops - Home, your Library, and your profile, drawn as your own AniList avatar. Switching between them springs rather than cuts: the selected tab grows the name of the page it belongs to, exactly as the title sheet's own capsule does, because it is the same control. Back from any of the three lands on Home instead of walking back through every tab visited, a repeat tap on the tab you are already on does nothing, and returning to a page restores what it was showing. The bar draws itself only over those pages: a screen opened from one of them - Settings, the tier list, a studio, somebody else's profile - keeps the whole screen.
- The Library is your own page now, not a tab of every profile: The list was the fourth tab of every profile, including a stranger's, which made the thing you consult most often one tap deeper than the thing you consult least - and it spent a tab of every profile on the one list that profile was least likely to be opened for. It is now the app's second page: your own anime and manga as posters, with the same type, filter, sort and search as before, and the same memory - the view you left it on and the place in it are still there when you come back. The profile kept what a profile is for: the person, their activity, their numbers, and their social graph. A profile no longer draws the Library chip at all, and every profile is four tabs instead of five.
- A profile's own pages sit under its top bar: With the app's bar at the bottom edge, the profile could not keep a second capsule against the same edge - two bars stacked is two answers to one question. Home, Activity, Stats and Social now switch from directly under the profile's top bar, where they read as the sections of one page rather than as places to go. And the two ways into your own profile agree: the avatar in the dashboard's top bar, the avatar on the Library page, and the face on the bar are one tap to one screen.
